# Getting Started with Hugging Face: Explore AI Models and Demos

> **In short:** Hugging Face is a website where people and companies share AI models and demo apps. You can browse the models, try some of them right on their page, and open interactive demos called Spaces, all in your browser.

Curious about AI but not sure where to start? Hugging Face lets you see many different AI tools in action without installing anything. By the end of this guide, you'll know how to find a model, try it when its page offers a widget, and use a Space.

## Before you start

- **A web browser** on a computer, tablet, or phone.
- **A Hugging Face account (optional at first).** You can browse without one. Some features may ask you to sign in; you can sign up at [huggingface.co](https://huggingface.co).
- **About 10–15 minutes.**

## Step 1: Open the models page

Go to [huggingface.co/models](https://huggingface.co/models). An **AI model** is a program trained to do a task, such as sorting text, generating images, or turning speech into text. This page lists models that the community has shared.

You'll know it worked when you see a long list of models with names, task labels, and download counts.

## Step 2: Find a model for a task

Use the search box or the task filters on the models page to narrow the list, for example to text classification or summarization. Each model has a page with a description written by its authors, called a model card.

💬 Example: Search for "sentiment" to find models that guess whether a sentence sounds positive or negative.

You'll know it worked when the list shows models related to your task.

## Step 3: Try a model in its widget

Hugging Face's docs say many model pages have a **widget** that lets anyone run the model in the browser. Widgets are powered by Inference Providers, and a widget only appears when at least one provider serves that model, so not every model has one. If a page has a widget, type or upload your input and run it. Some widgets offer example inputs you can pick from a list.

Running a widget uses Inference Providers. Hugging Face's pricing page says free accounts don't include monthly credits for them, so a widget may ask you to sign in, buy credits, or upgrade. If that happens, try a Space instead (Step 4): Hugging Face says ZeroGPU Spaces are free to use for everyone, with a daily usage quota.

If the model you picked has no widget, go back and choose another one. The [models page filtered by Inference Provider](https://huggingface.co/models?inference_provider=all&sort=trending) shows models that do.

You'll know it worked when the widget shows the model's result, such as a label with a score or a generated text.

## Step 4: Explore a Space

A **Space** is a small web app built around one or more AI models. Go to [huggingface.co/spaces](https://huggingface.co/spaces), search for something you'd like to try, such as image generation or speech to text, and open a Space. The app runs right on its page. If it hasn't been used for a while, it may need a moment to start.

💬 Example: Open the Space [openai/whisper](https://huggingface.co/spaces/openai/whisper), upload a short voice recording, and click **Submit** to turn it into text.

You'll know it worked when the app on the page responds to your input.

## Step 5: Keep your results

Spaces and widgets show your result on the page, but you shouldn't count on it being saved. If you want to keep it, use the download or copy option the app offers, or copy the text yourself and paste it into a document.

You'll know it worked when your result is saved on your device.

## Common mistakes

- **Expecting every model to have a try-it box.** Widgets only appear for models served by an Inference Provider. *The fix:* Pick a model with a widget, or try a Space instead.
- **Uploading private files.** Many demos are public apps run by other people. *The fix:* Use test files and don't upload anything confidential.
- **Giving up when a Space is slow.** Free Spaces can sleep when unused and take a moment to wake up. *The fix:* Wait a little, then refresh, or try another Space.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** You can try AI tools for things like transcribing a voice memo or checking the tone of a sentence, right in your browser.
- **For your business or work:** You can quickly see what kinds of AI models exist for a task before you decide what to build or buy.
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with a Space. It's the easiest way to see a model working, with buttons instead of settings.

## Try it now

Go to [huggingface.co/spaces](https://huggingface.co/spaces), search for "speech to text," open one Space, and try it with a 10-second recording of your own voice.
